title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella remains confident in Nvidia after Huang’s exit
content:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella weighed in on former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s unexpected departure amid a series of shocking controversies.
“It’s all sort of pretty tragic in the sense of, you know, Jensen is somebody I’ve known for a long time. I’ve admired what he’s done, and at this point, I kind of want to give him space to figure this out,” Nadella said onstage at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday.
Huang stepped down last week from his CEO role, which he has held for 33 years. Huang’s leadership has been central to Nvidia’s ascent to one of the world’s most valuable companies, but his judgment was questioned after it was reported that he had an affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom U.S. officials believe is a Chinese spy feeding information back to Beijing. It was also revealed that Huang was having affairs with two Nvidia employees, including one who was a direct report.
While the world waits to see what the long-term economic impacts of Huang’s departure might be, Nadella says he still has confidence in Nvidia, which is a close partner of Microsoft.
“I’ll just say this one thing,” Nadella added. “Colette [Kress, interim CEO at Nvidia] worked at Microsoft for a long time. I’ve known her for a long time. She’s a tremendous person… I’m in touch with the same set of people I was in touch with before [Huang left], so I have a lot of confidence in the Nvidia team and their ability to continue to do the good work.”
Microsoft is not unlike Nvidia in that its founder Bill Gates inhabited a larger-than-life persona as CEO.
“Founders are unbelievable in the sense that they create something from nothing, so that is pretty magical… They’re singular, but they’re not gods, right?” Nadella said. “I used to say to Bill [Gates]… Founders also die, and so at some point, a company, if it needs to succeed, it has to have someone take over.”

report.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says he remains confident in Nvidia after Jensen Huang’s abrupt exit, praising interim CEO Colette Kress and the team.
report.background: Jensen Huang led Nvidia for 33 years, turning it from a graphics-chip maker into the central supplier of GPUs for the AI boom. Nvidia’s chips power Microsoft Azure, OpenAI, and most major AI models, making its stability important far beyond the company. Huang stepped down after reports of an affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom U.S. officials reportedly suspect of being a Chinese spy, and relationships with Nvidia employees, including a direct report. The controversy raises governance, national-security, and succession questions for a founder-led company. Nadella, speaking at the New York Times DealBook Summit, compared founder-led firms to Microsoft under Bill Gates: founders are singular but not gods, and eventually someone else must take over.
key_points: Huang’s exit follows reports of personal-conduct controversies: an alleged affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom U.S. officials reportedly suspect of spying for China, and relationships with Nvidia employees, including a direct report. The revelations raised governance and national-security concerns at a company central to AI infrastructure.

Nadella called the situation “pretty tragic,” said he has long admired Huang, and wants to give him space to figure things out. But he stopped short of defending Huang’s conduct, focusing instead on Nvidia’s team and business continuity.

Nadella cited interim CEO Colette Kress’s long tenure at Microsoft and his personal relationship with her as reasons for confidence. He said his contacts at Nvidia are unchanged, signaling continuity in the Microsoft-Nvidia partnership.

Nadella reflected on founder-led companies, saying founders create something from nothing but are “not gods.” He noted that founders eventually leave and companies must have successors ready if they are to keep succeeding.
report.impact: Nvidia’s leadership turmoil matters because the AI industry depends on its GPUs and software ecosystem. Any perceived instability could affect partner confidence, supply commitments, and strategic decisions at Microsoft, OpenAI, and cloud providers. For developers, the CUDA ecosystem is likely to remain stable in the short term, but uncertainty may accelerate interest in AMD, custom silicon, and open-source inference stacks. Regular users may see little immediate change, yet longer-term shifts in Nvidia’s roadmap, pricing, or support could influence AI service costs and availability. Microsoft’s public confidence is a signal that major customers want continuity, not disruption.
report.tools: To follow Nvidia’s ecosystem, watch CUDA, TensorRT, and Nvidia NIM for inference. Microsoft Azure AI and Azure Machine Learning show how cloud partners adapt. For open-source alternatives, track vLLM, Triton Inference Server, PyTorch, and AMD ROCm as competing or complementary stacks for GPU-based AI workloads.
